cards.text: Meanwhile, Jesus' apostles gather around Him and tell Him all they've done and taught. But so many people are coming and going that they don't even have time to eat. That's the kind of day where your cookie is still sitting on your desk at quitting time with ONE bite out of it.

cards.question: With people everywhere and no time to eat, Jesus tells His apostles to come away with Him to a solitary place and ___ for a while.

cards.text: So they get in a boat and head off by themselves to a solitary place. Peace and quiet. FINALLY.

cards.question: Lots of people see Jesus and the apostles leaving in the boat and recognize them. What do those people do?

answers.text: Run there on foot and get there first
Wait on the shore for the boat to come back
Go back home to their own towns

cards.text: Jesus steps ashore at the quiet getaway, and there's a large crowd waiting. That's like sneaking out to your car for five quiet minutes and finding the whole office already in the back seat.

cards.question: Jesus has compassion on the crowd, because they're like sheep without a ___.
Jesus came to this place to rest. True or false: when He sees the crowd, He sends them away and gets back in the boat.

cards.text: Instead, Jesus teaches them many things. By now it's late, and the disciples come to Him and say, "This is a desolate place, and the hour is already late."

cards.question: It's late and they're out in a desolate place. True or false: the disciples want Jesus to send the crowd off to the villages to buy something to eat.

cards.text: But Jesus tells them, "You give them something to eat." I bet the disciples looked at each other like the boss just volunteered them to throw the whole company party, TONIGHT.

cards.question: The disciples ask Jesus if they should go buy bread for all these people. How much money do they mention spending?

cards.text: So Jesus sends them to go see how many loaves they have.

cards.question: The disciples check what food they have for the crowd. What do they come back with?

answers.text: Seven loaves and a few fish
Twenty barley loaves and fresh grain

cards.text: Then Jesus has the disciples get the people sitting down on the green grass. Friend, that's walking into a stadium with ONE cookie and telling everybody, "Go ahead and get comfortable."

cards.question: Jesus has the disciples get everyone seated on the green grass. How do the people sit down?

answers.text: In groups of hundreds and fifties
In one long line along the shore
In twelve groups by their tribes

cards.text: Then Jesus takes the five loaves and the two fish, looks up to heaven and speaks a blessing.

cards.question: Jesus breaks the loaves. True or false: He gives the pieces to His disciples to set before the people.

cards.text: He divides the two fish among them all, and they ALL eat and are satisfied. My ovens run every single day, friend, and I have NEVER fed a crowd like that.

cards.question: After everyone eats, the disciples pick up ___ basketfuls of broken pieces of bread and fish.
Here's the final head count from five loaves and two fish. How many men ate the loaves?

findings.problem: The passage opens with "Meanwhile" and the apostles reporting "all they had done and taught", which is the middle of a thought. The card keeps "Meanwhile" but never says what came before. The baker isn't told that Jesus had sent the apostles out (Mark 6:7-13), so "Meanwhile" and the report have no context.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to finish the line "like sheep without a ___", which is wording they haven't seen. Nothing earlier sets up a shepherd, and "pasture" or "fold" would also make sense here, especially with a hungry crowd. The baker can't reason out the right word from the earlier cards. The question should ask about the meaning of the picture, not the next word of the line.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
